covers: Capture from process streams where the CO2 is already concentrated and nitrogen-free: shifted syngas and acid-gas removal in ammonia, methanol and hydrogen plants (including upgrader hydrogen units), formation CO2 removed at gas-processing plants, fermentation CO2 at ethanol plants, pre-combustion capture on gasifiers, oxygen-blown iron routes (HIsarna, smelting reduction, syngas DRI, top-gas recycling), indirectly heated calciners, oxy-fuel flue gas. cims-services: Chemical Products.CCS is costed as this case (1.0 GJ natural gas/t CO2, capex 153 $ per t-per-yr, 100% removal) and serves Ammonia Methanol 'Adv reforming reactors CCS'; Petroleum Refining.CCS as requested by Hydrogen 'NG steam reforming Eff CCS' and 'petcoke gasification CCS'; Iron and Steel.CCS as requested by Molten Steel.Integrated 'HIsarna CCS', 'DRI + EAF + CCS', 'Smelter + EAF + CCS', 'Corex smelter + CCS', 'Top gas recycling CCS'; Natural Gas.Production.Supply.Formation CO2 'Formation CCS'; Petroleum Crude.CCS as requested by Hydrogen 'SMR CCS' and Bitumen.Upgrading 'Upgrading ELDAR CCS'
harmonized-now: capture-unit (IPCC 'CCUS of concentrated CO2'); capture-unit_hydrogen; capture-unit_methanol; capture-unit_top-gas-recycling-ccs
note: IPCC Table 11.3: 99% reduction, TRL 9, <= USD40/t, available today; footnote f calls disposal of concentrated CO2 at USD15-40/t well established. IPCC names HIsarna and syngas DRI as concentrated; smelting reduction, Corex and top-gas recycling are put here by analogy (oxygen-blown, nitrogen-free gas) and need a source. An SMR has both kinds: process CO2 from the shift is concentrated, the reformer furnace flue is dilute. CIMS books one rate for it. Integrated routes (hisarna-ccs, shaft-furnace_syngas_ccs, calciner_ccs) stay on their sector end use as technology choices; this end use is the capture service they draw on. CIMS has no capture option on ethanol fermentation CO2; its Ethanol.CCS serves only boilers. Sector and cross-sector rows named `<host>_ccs-concentrated` point here: the capture plant's cost and energy are held on this end use once and are not repeated on the host row, which carries only the host-side effects.

note: Added 2026-09-15, split from fugitive emissions the same day. Deliberate disposal: the volume is event- and equipment-driven and largely metered or estimated per event, and the abatement is equipment substitution. The service is really tonnes of methane; the unit is the gas disposed of on an energy basis, so it sits beside the other end uses. Flaring competes with venting as a destruction route, which is why the two stay together.

note: Split from venting and flaring, 2026-09-15. Leaks scale with component count and stock age rather than with throughput, the volume is inferred from emission factors or top-down measurement rather than metered, and the abatement is a programme - survey frequency, monitoring, low-emission components - not a device that competes with a vapour recovery unit. Canadian methane regulations set LDAR frequency separately from venting limits. Top-down measurement often cannot attribute observed methane between unburnt flare gas, venting and leaks; where a source does not attribute it, say so rather than splitting on an assumption.
